posts.title: First post
posts.body: Hello world, this is my very first post on this platform. I wanted to share my excitement about starting this journey into web development. At first it feels overwhelming, but with consistent practice I’m confident it will all make sense. This post marks the beginning of many more to come.

posts.title: React Journey
posts.body: Started learning React today, and honestly it feels amazing. JSX looked strange at first, but once I wrote my first functional component it started to click. My plan is to build small projects like a to-do app, a weather app, and then eventually move to something bigger. Consistency will be the key to mastering React.

posts.title: TailwindCSS Fun
posts.body: TailwindCSS is such a game changer for me. Instead of switching back and forth between CSS files and my JSX code, I can apply classes directly. Utility-first styling felt confusing initially, but now I see how fast it makes development. I built a card component in minutes and it looked clean right away.

posts.title: API with Node.js
posts.body: Today I created my first backend API using Node.js and Express. I was surprised at how little code it took to set up routes, handle requests, and return JSON data. My next step is connecting it with MongoDB so I can store data permanently. It feels great to see both frontend and backend coming together.

posts.title: Debugging Tips
posts.body: Debugging used to mean endless console.log statements for me, but then I discovered the power of VS Code’s built-in debugger. Setting breakpoints, inspecting variables, and stepping through code line by line has saved me hours. If you’re still spamming console.log, trust me, try the debugger instead.

posts.title: Frontend vs Backend
posts.body: Many beginners often wonder what the difference between frontend and backend is. Frontend deals with the parts of an application that the user interacts with directly, such as UI components, buttons, and layouts. Backend, on the other hand, is all about handling data, authentication, and business logic. Both are important for full-stack development, and learning each side gives you a much deeper perspective on web apps.

posts.title: My First Database Connection
posts.body: Today I connected my app to a database for the first time! I used MongoDB Atlas for cloud hosting, and it was surprisingly straightforward to set up. Just a connection string, some environment variables, and my backend API was ready to store and retrieve data. It feels like I unlocked a huge new level of possibilities.

posts.title: Authentication Basics
posts.body: Authentication has always been a scary topic for me. But today I built a simple login system with JWT tokens, and I finally understand the flow: the user logs in, gets a token, and uses it to access protected routes. Security is still a big topic to learn, but at least I feel confident with the basics now.

posts.title: State Management with Redux
posts.body: Redux was one of the hardest concepts for me to understand when starting out. Actions, reducers, and the store felt abstract and confusing. But once I built a simple counter app and then a todo app with Redux, it finally started making sense. Now I appreciate how Redux centralizes state and makes debugging much easier.

posts.title: Dark Mode Everywhere
posts.body: I added dark mode to my app today, and it was so satisfying. With TailwindCSS, switching themes was as simple as toggling a class. Users really appreciate dark mode, and it also makes apps look modern instantly.

posts.title: Deploying to Vercel
posts.body: I just deployed my first app on Vercel, and it was incredibly simple. I connected my GitHub repo, selected the project, and within minutes it was live. Having CI/CD automatically handle builds and deployments feels magical compared to uploading files manually.

posts.title: Learning TypeScript
posts.body: JavaScript is fun, but TypeScript makes it safer and easier to scale. Adding types to my functions and props has already caught a lot of mistakes before runtime. At first the syntax looked verbose, but I now see the huge benefits in long-term projects.

posts.title: CSS Grid Layouts
posts.body: I finally tried CSS Grid for building layouts, and it feels so much cleaner than floats or flexbox hacks. Defining rows and columns explicitly gives me complete control. I built a photo gallery in under 20 minutes that looked perfectly aligned on all screens.

posts.title: Building a Weather App
posts.body: For practice, I built a weather app using an open API. It fetches live weather data, displays temperature, and even shows different icons based on the weather condition. It felt so satisfying to make an app that pulls in real-world data and updates instantly.

posts.title: Learning Docker Basics
posts.body: Docker seemed intimidating at first, but once I learned about images and containers, things started to make sense. Now I can run my app in a container, ship it anywhere, and it just works the same. This makes development and deployment so much smoother.

posts.title: GraphQL vs REST
posts.body: After working with REST APIs for a long time, I tried GraphQL. It felt strange at first, but I loved being able to fetch exactly the data I needed in a single query. No more over-fetching or under-fetching. For complex apps, GraphQL is a game changer.

posts.title: Performance Optimization
posts.body: Optimizing performance is often underrated. Lazy loading images, memoizing components in React, and using useCallback/useMemo correctly made my app way faster. Tools like Lighthouse also give great insights for improvements.

posts.title: Building a Chat App
posts.body: Today I started building a real-time chat app using Socket.IO. Sending and receiving messages instantly felt amazing to see in action. Real-time apps are tricky, but once set up, they feel magical for users.

posts.title: REST API Error Handling
posts.body: Good error handling in APIs is underrated. Returning proper status codes, descriptive error messages, and consistent error structures helps frontend developers a lot. I recently refactored my API to handle errors better, and debugging became way easier.

posts.title: Exploring Next.js
posts.body: Next.js is such a powerful framework. From file-based routing to SSR and API routes, it feels like a complete package for React developers. I deployed a test app and was blown away by how fast it was with static site generation.

posts.title: Custom Hooks in React
posts.body: Custom hooks are such a neat feature of React. I created a useFetch hook that handles API calls and state management. It keeps my components much cleaner and reusable. Hooks really changed the way I think about building apps.

posts.title: Learning Prisma ORM
posts.body: Prisma makes working with databases so much easier. Its type-safe client and schema-based approach reduce a lot of boilerplate. I used it with PostgreSQL, and the experience was smooth. No more writing endless SQL queries manually.

posts.title: Microservices Architecture
posts.body: Today I read about microservices architecture. Breaking down apps into smaller services that communicate over APIs makes scaling easier. It’s more complex than monoliths, but the flexibility and resilience it offers is impressive.
